question: Who Owns Taco Bell?
quick_answer: Taco Bell is owned by Yum! Brands, a publicly traded company that is also the parent of KFC and Pizza Hut. Taco Bell was founded in 1962 by Glen Bell in Downey, California, and became part of the company that is now Yum! Brands, which was spun off from PepsiCo in 1997.
key_facts: Sister brands: KFC and Pizza Hut
Yum! Brands was spun off from PepsiCo in 1997

body.heading: Who owns Taco Bell?
body.text: Taco Bell is part of Yum! Brands, one of the world's largest restaurant companies. Yum! Brands is publicly traded and also owns KFC and Pizza Hut, so Taco Bell shares a parent with two other huge fast-food names.

body.heading: How it got there
body.text: Taco Bell was founded in 1962 by Glen Bell in Downey, California. PepsiCo bought it in 1978 and ran it alongside KFC and Pizza Hut. In 1997, PepsiCo spun off its restaurant business, which became Tricon and was later renamed Yum! Brands, the company that still owns Taco Bell today.

body.heading: What that means for diners
body.text: Because Taco Bell sits under Yum! Brands with KFC and Pizza Hut, you will sometimes see shared locations or combined restaurants with those brands. Taco Bell keeps its own Mexican-inspired menu and identity under that corporate umbrella.

faqs.q: Is Taco Bell owned by the same company as KFC?
faqs.a: Yes. Taco Bell, KFC and Pizza Hut are all owned by Yum! Brands.
